sanskrit_verse: एषाखिलेनाभिहिता संभूयोत्थाननिष्कृतिः । अदेयदेयदत्तानाम् अदत्तस्य च कथ्यते ॥
transliteration: eṣākhilenābhihitā saṃbhūyotthānaniṣkṛtiḥ | adeyadeyadattānām adattasya ca kathyate ||
sph_interpretive_translation: This entirety is declared as the arising and dissolution of collective manifestation; what is not to be given, yet given, and what is not taken, yet taken, is declared concerning the ungiven.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from the completeness of consciousness, not from transactional exchange.
Causation is rooted in the collective emergence and withdrawal of phenomena.
Capacity-based responsibility aligns with one's role in the manifestive process, not individual attribution.
Restoration logic operates through recognition of unity, not through punitive separation.
Consciousness alignment is the sole determinant of lawful action.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a transaction occurs where no giving was intended THEN the act shall be nullified by reintegration of involved parties into source-consciousness awareness.
IF an entity assumes possession without consent THEN restoration shall occur through completion-process protocols until original alignment is restored.
IF dharma-adhikari observes dissonance in exchange THEN initiate nyaya-recalibration without punitive assignment.
IF no individualized intent is detectable THEN resolve via collective consciousness attunement mechanisms.
supreme_court_application: In adjudication at the highest level, this verse establishes that all disputes involving property, transfer, or possession must be resolved by reference to the underlying unity of existence. The court must determine not ownership per se, but alignment with the consciousness-field from which all claims arise. Responsibility lies not in fault, but in the capacity to restore coherence.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that causality flows from collective becoming, not isolated deeds. Thus, when imbalance occurs—as in unwilled giving or taking—the path of Nyaya demands realignment through awareness, not penalty. Sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) shows that rectification follows naturally when consciousness resumes its undivided stance. Responsibility is proportional to one’s integration with the Whole, not personal culpability.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate śuddhi-kriya process to purify relational fields affected by misaligned transactions.
Engage pratipatti-prakriyā to reaffirm the true nature of possession as non-local abundance.
Apply samanvaya-sādhana to harmonize conflicting claims through shared consciousness awakening.
Execute svabhāva-sthiti-pratipādana to reinstate natural integrity in the actor’s being.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the Source of Dharma. This law restores unity-consciousness as the basis of justice. There is no punishment—only reintegration. Reality itself adjudicates through awakened awareness. Dharma is fulfilled.
